questions.question: What is the primary function of an AND gate in digital logic?
options: Its output is true if at least one of its inputs is true.
Its output is the inverse of its single input.
Its output is true only if all of its inputs are true.
Its output is true if its inputs are different.
Its output is true if its inputs are the same.

questions.question: In a typical Central Processing Unit (CPU) datapath, what is the primary function of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)?
options: To fetch instructions from the main memory.
To store program instructions and data temporarily.
To control the sequence of operations within the CPU.
To perform arithmetic operations (e.g., addition, subtraction) and logical operations (e.g., AND, OR).
To manage communication between the CPU and I/O devices.

questions.question: In the physical design phase of an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC), what is the primary objective of the 'Placement' step?
options: To create a high-level behavioral description of the circuit.
To verify the logical correctness of the design using formal methods.
To convert the Register Transfer Level (RTL) code into a gate-level netlist.
To determine the optimal physical locations for all standard cells and macro blocks on the silicon die.
To connect the various components of the circuit with metal wires according to the netlist.

questions.question: What is the primary distinction between a 'write-through' and a 'write-back' cache policy regarding memory updates?
options: Write-through updates main memory immediately upon a write hit, while write-back delays updating main memory until the cache block is evicted or explicitly flushed.
Write-back updates main memory immediately upon a write hit, while write-through delays updating main memory until the cache block is evicted or explicitly flushed.
Write-through caches are only used for instruction memory, whereas write-back caches are only used for data memory.
Write-back caches are simpler to implement and consume less power than write-through caches.
Write-through policies inherently provide better performance for frequently modified data than write-back policies.

questions.question: In complex System-on-Chip (SoC) designs, especially those with many heterogeneous processing elements, what is the primary advantage of employing a Network-on-Chip (NoC) architecture over a traditional shared bus interconnect?
options: NoCs inherently simplify the debugging process for hardware and software interfaces.
NoCs primarily reduce the overall static power consumption of the SoC.
NoCs provide significantly better scalability in terms of bandwidth and latency as the number of communicating intellectual property (IP) blocks increases.
NoCs allow for dynamic reconfiguration of IP blocks at runtime, which is impossible with bus-based systems.
NoCs are exclusively used for off-chip communication between multiple interconnected SoCs.
